newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Napocor may sell stake in units.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Napocor may sell stake in units.

text.p: National Power Co (Napocor) is considering the sale of up to 30 percent in seven generation and one transmission companies to strategic partners as part of its privatisation plan, Napocor president Guido Delgado said.

In an interview with Reuters on Wednesday, Delgado said, "It might be too premature to say but we plan to offer up to 30 percent of the genco (generation companies) including the transco (transmission company) to strategic partners."
In January, the state-owned power firm said it planned to set up seven power-generating companies and sell them to the private sector as part of its privatisation.
Delgado said the search for a partner will have to be approved by the Department of Finance and the Cabinet-level Committee on Privatisation.
The rest of the shares will be offered to the public and about 10 percent to employees.
Delgado could not say how much the privatisation exercise would raise, noting that studies on the company's valuations are still being done.
Details on the stock sale have also not been finalised, as the privatisation exercise itself depends on passage by Congress of an electricity sector restructuring bill.
The bill, which sets down guidelines for privatising the firm, is expected to be passed within the year.
Napocor has dominated the country's electricity sector for 60 years. At the end of 1996, its total assets amounted to 458.195 billion pesos, according to its latest balance sheet.
Under the privatisation plan, existing power plants will be grouped under each generation company based on financial viability, geography and perceived investor preferences among other criteria.
The move to privatise should reap savings of $6 billion over 10 years, Napocor estimated.
The utility decided to seek outside investors as its estimated $1.4 billion per year power infrastructure investment could not be provided for by the national government.
